scotia_sea.name: Scotia Sea
scotia_sea.remarks: Rough water between South America and the Antarctic Peninsula, and the crossing every ship to Antarctica has to make.

argentina.name: Argentina
argentina.remarks: Cold Atlantic water with southern right whales calving off Peninsula Valdes, and sea lions that will happily join a dive uninvited.

bolivia.name: Bolivia
bolivia.remarks: Landlocked since 1904 and visibly unresigned to it — the country still maintains a navy, which operates on Lake Titicaca at nearly four thousand metres.

brazil.name: Brazil
brazil.remarks: Seven and a half thousand kilometres of coast, plus freshwater springs inland at Bonito where the visibility runs to fifty metres through submerged forest.

chile.name: Chile
chile.remarks: Four thousand kilometres long and rarely more than two hundred wide. Cold Humboldt water the whole way, and Easter Island a very long way offshore with the clearest water in the Pacific.

colombia.name: Colombia
colombia.remarks: Coast on two oceans with completely different water. Malpelo, off the Pacific side, gathers hammerheads by the hundred.

ecuador.name: Ecuador
ecuador.remarks: The smallest Andean country, and the one that happens to own the Galapagos.

galapagos_islands.name: Galapagos Islands
galapagos_islands.remarks: Cold upwelling arrives at the equator here, which is why a diver can meet penguins and hammerheads on the same dive. The water is colder than anyone expects and the wetsuit should reflect that.

guyana.name: Guyana
guyana.remarks: A coast of silt and mangrove, with most of the country forest behind it.

paraguay.name: Paraguay
paraguay.remarks: Landlocked, and reaching the sea only by river — which has not stopped it having a navy either.

peru.name: Peru
peru.remarks: The Humboldt Current runs cold and rich along the whole coast, supporting one of the largest fisheries in the world and water few people dive without a good suit.

suriname.name: Suriname
suriname.remarks: The smallest sovereign state in South America, and largely rainforest.

uruguay.name: Uruguay
uruguay.remarks: Where the Rio de la Plata meets the Atlantic, in an estuary wide enough to be mistaken for the sea itself.

venezuela.name: Venezuela
venezuela.remarks: A long Caribbean coast, with Los Roques offshore — an atoll-like archipelago of shallow reef and sand.

french_guiana.name: French Guiana
french_guiana.remarks: An overseas department of France, and therefore the only part of the European Union on the South American mainland.

falkland_islands.name: Falkland Islands
falkland_islands.remarks: Cold, windy and surrounded by kelp forest, with more penguins than people by a considerable margin.
